claims.text: Existing uncertainty estimation approaches for LLMs are either white-box or computationally demanding.

The proposed non-parametric uncertainty quantification method efficiently estimates point-wise dependencies between input and decision on the fly with a single inference without access to token logits.
The proposed estimator informs the statistical interpretation of decision trustworthiness.
The decision-making agent prompts users for preferences when more than one action has high estimated point-wise dependencies.
The proposed uncertainty estimation and decision-making agent design offer a cost-efficient approach for AI agent development.

evidence.description: Existing approaches are either white-box or computationally demanding, limiting use of black-box proprietary LLMs within budgets.

methodologies.name: Non-Parametric Uncertainty Quantification for Black-Box LLMs
methodologies.description: Estimates point-wise dependencies between input and decision on the fly using a single inference without token logits.

methodologies.name: Uncertainty-Aware Decision-Making Agent
methodologies.description: Generates actions based on user prompts and requests user preferences when multiple actions have high estimated point-wise dependencies.

limitations.text: Existing approaches are either white-box or computationally demanding, limiting use of black-box proprietary LLMs within budgets.
